label: Montebore
note: Shaped as stacked rounds of decreasing diameter, after the ruined tower of Montebore castle; served at the 1489 wedding of Isabella of Aragon

about.text: Montebore is a raw-milk cheese from the Tortona hills of Piedmont, built from stacked rounds like a tiered cake. It is mentioned in the 12th century, was served at a Sforza wedding in 1489, and had practically died out by 1982 before one old maker taught it to a new generation; it is now a Slow Food Presidium.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

Raw mixed cow (60-75%) and sheep milk; eaten fresh at 20 days, medium at 45-60 days, aged at 4-5 months (ONAF, Gambero Rosso); rind forms after about 5-6 days. Wedding-cake shape. Slow Food presidium, status reported lapsed after the producer cooperative failed in 2021

facts.v: Today about 70–75 % cow's and 25–30 % sheep's milk; sheep's only in the past
